subject: Social Habits
title: Telling the truth
subtopics: Telling the truth when something goes wrong
Being brave to say the truth
objectives: Children will say what is true about simple pictures and events.
Children will tell an adult the truth about a small accident with support.
content: What is true, telling the truth when something goes wrong, and being brave to say the truth.
teachingActivities: Toddlers mix pretend and real, so teach "true" with simple real facts; never trap a child into lying by asking "Did you do it?" when you know; thank children for telling the truth even when they made a mess; respond calmly; use stories and puppets.
learnerActivities: Say what is true about simple pictures and events and tell an adult about a spill or mistake.
resources: Picture cards showing true and not-true things
assessment: Observe whether each child says what is true about a simple event and tells an adult about a mistake.
expectedOutcomes: Says what is true about a simple event.
Tells an adult about a spill or mistake.

lessons.title: What is true?
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will say whether a simple statement about a picture is true.
successCriteria: Says true or not true with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can say sorry, help others and do small jobs.
resources: Picture cards of a dog, a cat, a car and a tree
lessons.starter: Show a picture of a dog and say "This is a dog. That is true." Then say "This is a fish. That is not true."
teacherActivities: Show a picture and say a true sentence.
Show a picture and say a silly untrue sentence.
Let each child say a true thing about a picture.
learnerActivities: Children say not true and laugh.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show a picture and say a true sentence. Children: Children say true.
Step 2. Teacher: Show a picture and say a silly untrue sentence. Children: Children say not true and laugh.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child say a true thing about a picture. Children: Child says a true thing.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "We tell what is true." Children: Children repeat the sentence.

practical.title: True or not true
practical.safety: Keep the examples silly and safe and never make a child feel wrong. Accept pretend play as pretend.

differentiation.support: Offer two pictures and say which is true.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say a true sentence about the room.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Says true or not true with support
Says a true thing about a picture
lessons.conclusion: Sing the truth song and wave.
lessons.homeConnection: Play a true or not true game at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say whether a simple statement about a picture is true" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Tell the truth, tell the truth, it is the best thing to do.

lessons.title: Telling the truth about a spill
lessons.subject: Social Habits
lessons.subtopic: Telling the truth when something goes wrong
objectives: Children will tell an adult when they spill or break something by accident.
successCriteria: Says oops and tells an adult
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can say sorry, help others and do small jobs.
resources: A plastic cup of water on a tray
lessons.starter: Show the puppet spilling a cup and say "Oops! The puppet tells the teacher."
teacherActivities: Show the puppet telling the teacher in a small voice.
Say "Thank you for telling me" calmly and wipe the spill.
Let each child pretend to spill and tell the teacher.
Say "Accidents happen. We tell the truth."
learnerActivities: Children watch and say thank you.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the puppet telling the teacher in a small voice. Children: Children watch and say oops.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Thank you for telling me" calmly and wipe the spill. Children: Children watch and say thank you.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child pretend to spill and tell the teacher. Children: Child says oops and tells.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Accidents happen. We tell the truth." Children: Children repeat tell the truth.

practical.title: Oops and tell
steps: Spill a little water on a tray.
practical.safety: Use only a little water on a tray and wipe spills at once. Never scold a child who tells the truth about an accident.

differentiation.support: Say oops together and tell the teacher.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell what happened in one sentence.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we say after a spill?

expectedOutcomes: Says oops and tells an adult
Understands that telling the truth is safe
lessons.conclusion: Wipe the table together and say thank you.
lessons.homeConnection: Thank your child for telling the truth even when they made a mess.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "tell an adult when they spill or break something by accident" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Being brave to tell the truth
lessons.subject: Social Habits
lessons.subtopic: Being brave to say the truth
objectives: Children will see that telling the truth is brave and makes people trust us.
successCriteria: Says that telling the truth is good
Joins a story about telling the truth
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can say sorry, help others and do small jobs.
lessons.starter: Tell a very short story: "Kemi broke a cup. She was scared. She told her mother the truth. Mother said thank you for telling me."
teacherActivities: Tell the story with pictures slowly.
Ask "How did Kemi feel at first?"
Give a brave badge to the story and say "Truth is brave."
learnerActivities: Child says she told the truth.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Tell the story with pictures slowly. Children: Children listen and look.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "How did Kemi feel at first?" Children: Child says scared.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "What did Kemi do?" Children: Child says she told the truth.
Step 4. Teacher: Give a brave badge to the story and say "Truth is brave." Children: Children clap and cheer.

practical.title: Story and badge
practical.safety: Use a gentle story with a kind ending. Never use frightening punishments in stories.

differentiation.support: Tell the story in two sentences with pictures.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say what they would do.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Understands that telling the truth is brave
lessons.homeConnection: Read a story about honesty and talk about it.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "see that telling the truth is brave and makes people trust us" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

pictures: A story picture of a girl and her mother

lessons.title: Truth and pretend
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will tell the difference between real and pretend in play.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can say sorry, help others and do small jobs.
resources: A real cup and a toy cup
Pictures of real and pretend things
lessons.starter: Hold a toy cup and say "This is a pretend cup. This one is a real cup."
teacherActivities: Show a real and a pretend object and name them.
Let children pretend to drink from a toy cup.
Say "Pretend is fun. Truth is real."
Sort pictures into real and pretend.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show a real and a pretend object and name them. Children: Children say real or pretend.
Step 2. Teacher: Let children pretend to drink from a toy cup. Children: Child pretends to drink.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "Pretend is fun. Truth is real." Children: Children repeat the sentence.
Step 4. Teacher: Sort pictures into real and pretend. Children: Child sorts a picture.

practical.title: Real and pretend
practical.safety: Use safe objects only. Keep play gentle and never call a child a liar for pretending.

differentiation.support: Offer two objects and say real or pretend.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a real thing and a pretend thing.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the toys away and say "Real or pretend."
lessons.homeConnection: Enjoy pretend play at home and name what is real.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "tell the difference between real and pretend in play" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 6 truth check
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child understands and says what is true.
successCriteria: Tells an adult about an accident
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can say sorry, help others and do small jobs.
lessons.starter: Sing the truth song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: true or not true, oops and tell, and real or pretend.
At each station watch how the child answers.
learnerActivities: Child answers with a word or action.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: true or not true, oops and tell, and real or pretend. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station watch how the child answers. Children: Child answers with a word or action.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Truth stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors dry. Never use a test that traps a child into a lie.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to say why we tell the truth.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: says true or not true; tells an adult about an accident; tells real from pretend; shows trust in adults.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 6
Says what is true with support
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep welcoming the truth at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child understands and says what is true" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
